en: Praise of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
the Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fata, by imperial decree.
I take refuge in the Omniscient One, the Teacher of all worlds,
the Great Dharma King, the Sage, whose hundred and eight names are an ocean of boundless merit and who is endowed with every auspiciousness.
Able to extinguish the sinful karma and afflictions of all sentient beings,
I now take refuge and pay homage to the one of universal great auspiciousness,
who delivers all living creatures and causes them to attain great peace and happiness.
I now take refuge and pay homage to the Compassionate One, the Honored One among bipeds,
who brings all auspicious matters to perfection for sentient beings.
I now take refuge and pay homage to the Unconditioned, the Supreme Honored One.
Having accomplished the state of the God of Gods, the profound meaning of the Great Illumination,
the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, who brings benefit and happiness to the world—
I shall now collect and proclaim those one hundred and eight supreme names.

If there is anyone who, at the break of dawn, gives rise to a heart of sincere resolve toward these one hundred and eight names—whether by reciting them, paying homage and mindfulness to them, memorizing and upholding them, or hearing them—they shall obtain the most supreme auspicious merit and virtue; all their afflictions and karmic offenses shall be swiftly purified; they shall not undergo further saṃsāra, but shall attain liberation and eventually achieve Buddhahood.
The name of this Great Muni’s virtues, which I now recite, chant, and venerate with mindfulness,
I universally dedicate to all sentient beings, so that together we may realize the fruit of Bodhi.
